beats.text: Every day, you repeat the same little moves on your PC.
Opening the same programs. Arranging the same windows. Hunting for the volume. Clicking through the same menus.
What if a {key}single key could do all of that? Or a {mouse}flick of the mouse? Or simply... {voice}your voice?

In these short videos, one for each feature, we'll see everything it can do. {commands}Commands, {quickmenus}QuickMenus, {events}events, {macros}macros and {kboard}K-Board. {voice}Voice control, your {phone}phone as a remote, and the {assistants}assistants that live on top of your windows.
K-Desktop is built around one simple idea: {command}the command.
A command is a {named}named sequence of actions. {open}Open a program, {wait}wait a second, {snap}snap its window to the left, {volume}set the volume to twenty percent. {steps}Step by step, in order.

And a command can be launched from almost anywhere. A {hotkey}hotkey or a {mouse}mouse button. A {quickmenu}QuickMenu, or the {launcher}launcher. Your {voice}voice, your {phone}phone, or the {network}network. {event}Something that happens on your PC. Or even an {assistant}assistant.
Around commands live a few companions. {macros}Macros that replay what you do. {kboard}K-Board profiles that remap your keys. And a {history}history that remembers every run.
It's a {portable}single portable program for {windows}Windows 10 and 11, in {languages}five languages. {local}Everything runs locally, and your {data}data stays in your own folder.
Let's start with the first one: {next}getting started.
